title: Clean up the answers
description: Check the riddle keeper's answers fairly, whatever capitals and spaces the player types, and tidy them for display.

tasks.title: Tools that come with every piece of text
tasks.body: Text has methods of its own: " Nova ".strip() is "Nova", "nova".upper() is "NOVA", and "a,b".split(",") is ["a", "b"]. A method never changes the text itself, because text cannot be changed: store what it gives back.
tasks.detail:
"a b".replace(" ", "") is "ab": replace() swaps every copy of one piece of text for another.

"nOVA".capitalize() is "Nova", a capital first letter and the rest lowercase; title() does that to every word.

split() with nothing in the brackets splits on any run of spaces, and " ".join(words) joins a list of words back with single spaces. f"{price:.2f}" shows a number with two decimal places.

tasks.code:
answer = "  The Moon "
clean = answer.strip().lower()
print(clean)
print(clean == "the moon")
print("map,rope,lamp".split(","))
print(" + ".join(["rope", "map"]))
print(f"{clean.title()} costs {2.5:.2f} coins")
tasks.output:
the moon
True
['map', 'rope', 'lamp']
rope + map
The Moon costs 2.50 coins
tasks.note: strip() and lower() tidy the reply before comparing it. split() makes a list, join() makes text again, and :.2f in the f-string writes 2.5 as 2.50.

tasks.question: After name = "nova", with name.upper() on a line of its own, what does print(name) show?
tasks.why: upper() gives back a new piece of text, which nothing stored. name still holds "nova".

tasks.prompt: Predict, then run: try " ".join(clean.split()) on "  lots   of   space ". Then change :.2f to :.1f.

Ask for the right answer to a riddle, then the player's answer.

1. They match if they are the same once capital letters and every space are ignored. Print correct or wrong.
2. Print the player's answer tidied: no spaces at either end, single spaces between words, and each word starting with a capital letter with the rest in lowercase.
tasks.starter: # Read the right answer and the reply, then compare and tidy
hints: To compare fairly, make both answers lowercase and take every space out with replace(), then use ==.
For the tidy version, split() the reply into words, which also drops extra spaces, capitalise each word, and join them back with single spaces.
With other names: label = title.replace(" ", "").lower() squashes a title, and " ".join(parts) puts a list back together with spaces.

error_hints.text: That method does not exist on text, or was called on a list. split() gives a list; join() is called on the text that goes between the words.
A name was used that has no value yet: check its spelling against the line where it was made.
join() needs a list of text. Make sure every item you join is text.
With The Moon and "  the moon ", the answers match once capitals and spaces are ignored: correct, then The Moon.
shadow and Shadows are different words, even ignoring capitals: wrong. The tidy version is Shadows.
ice cream and icecream match once every space is ignored, including the one inside.
Check an answer typed in capitals with extra spaces between words: tidy it to single spaces.
Check a reply of several words with odd spacing: each word gets its own capital.

similar_example.code:
title = "  The  Lost   Key "
label = title.replace(" ", "").lower()
parts = title.split()
print(label)
print(" ".join(parts))
similar_example.note: Squashing a title for comparing, and rebuilding it with single spaces. Your answers also need capitals fixed, word by word.

other_ways.code:
right = input("Answer? ")
reply = input("Reply? ")
squash = lambda text: "".join(text.split()).casefold()
print("correct" if squash(right) == squash(reply) else "wrong")
print(" ".join(word.capitalize() for word in reply.split()))
other_ways.note: "".join(text.split()) removes every space, and casefold() is a stronger lower() for comparing text in any language.

other_ways.code:
def tidy(text):
    return " ".join(w[:1].upper() + w[1:].lower() for w in text.split())

right = input("Answer? ")
reply = input("Reply? ")
same = tidy(right).replace(" ", "").lower() == tidy(reply).replace(" ", "").lower()
print("correct" if same else "wrong")
print(tidy(reply))
other_ways.note: Slices build each word: its first letter in capitals, and the rest in lowercase.
